FIRST DAY OF THE AUGUST 14-19 BREAK, which begins as the breaks.csv row forecast on the 13th -- both diet and training stop together. That row's end date remains an intention until the trip actually runs; correct it to what happened. THE 14TH IS A COMPLETE RECORD, CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER THE SAME EVENING -- the latte, two Patties Express patties, a Subway six-inch and about seven Kasugai gummies, and nothing else. 1,599 kcal and 95.6 g protein, which is 1,201 under the calorie target and 64 g under the protein floor, and both figures are real rather than a floor of unknown depth. The caution still stands for the 15th to the 19th, which have not happened: food eaten away from home tends to arrive estimated or not at all, so a low total on those days will need checking before it is believed.

No weigh-in this morning -- the last reading is the 188.2 of August 14, which is the pre-trip number the next one gets read against. 11:30pm to 8:00, 8 1/2 hours, the longest night of the break so far and in line with the 9 1/4 of the 14th; two long nights running after the 7 3/4 of the 13th reads as catch-up finishing rather than a change of pattern. SECOND DAY OF THE AUGUST 14-19 BREAK, and training was not nothing: fifteen minutes of the away-from-the-gym loaded-stretch routine, which is the one thing the trip section of the program asks for daily. Food came to 2,727 kcal and 94.0 g protein -- 73 OVER the calorie target and 66 g under the protein floor. That combination is the day's real finding and it is a different failure from the 14th's: the 14th was low on both (1,599 and 95.6), so it read as a light day, whereas the 15th hit the calorie target and still missed protein by the same margin. Two days in, protein is 95.6 and 94.0 against a 160 g floor while calories have gone from 1,201 under to 73 over, which says the gap is composition and not appetite. The evening is where it happens: cookie, tiramisu, juice, iced tea, three quarters of a pizza, peach crisp and ice cream came to about 1,325 kcal and 29 g of protein between them. Ten of the day's fourteen rows are estimates and the burger and the pizza carry about 890 kcal of the total, so this figure is softer than the 14th's, which was mostly published panels. THIS NOTE FIRST SAID 2,437 kcal AND 363 UNDER TARGET: that was written before dinner was fully reported, when the pizza was logged whole and the peach crisp and ice cream were not logged at all. The pizza was later corrected to three quarters.

No weigh-in this morning -- the last reading is still the 188.2 of August 14, the pre-trip number the next one gets read against. 11:30pm to 7:40, 8 hours 10 minutes, near-identical to the 8 1/2 of the 15th and the third straight night above eight after the 7 3/4 of the 13th; sleep on this trip is not the problem. THIRD DAY OF THE AUGUST 14-19 BREAK, and the away-from-the-gym routine ran again: all seven daily items at the prescribed doses, fifteen minutes, the same as the 15th. THIS NOTE FIRST SAID NO TRAINING WAS REPORTED AND THAT THE ROUTINE WENT UNDONE -- that was written before the session was mentioned and is wrong. Two runs in three trip days is the routine being served, which is what the trip section of the program asks for daily. BREAKFAST WAS SKIPPED, as stated on waking, and the day ran on lunch and dinner alone: 2,213 kcal and 91.0 g protein, 587 under the calorie target and 69 g under the protein floor. That is three consecutive days landing between 91 and 96 g of protein (95.6, then 94.0, then 91.0) against a 160 g floor, while calories swung 1,201 under, 73 over, 587 under. The protein figure is the stable one and the calorie figure is the noise, which is the clearest evidence yet that the shortfall is composition and not appetite. Dinner carried the day: four manicotti at an estimated 56 g of protein, more than any other single item of the trip, and without them the day lands in the thirties. The morning half of this note predicted that skipping breakfast would leave the whole 160 g floor to lunch and dinner and that dinner would not close a 133 g gap; it did not, missing by 69. Sodium came to 3,938 mg, the highest of the break, driven by the wraps (1,670) and the manicotti (1,680). EVERY ROW ON THIS DAY IS AN ESTIMATE -- seven rows, all source claude, not one published panel among them, which makes this the softest daily total of the run so far. The manicotti especially is a component build-up (shell, ricotta, mozzarella, parmesan, marinara) rather than an observed portion and carries roughly a 30% band, so its 56 g of protein could plausibly be 39 or 73.

No weigh-in this morning -- the last reading is still the 188.2 of August 14, the pre-trip number the next one gets read against, and there has now been no weigh-in for four days. 11pm to ~7:45, 8 hours 45 minutes, the fourth straight night above eight (8 1/2, 8 1/10, and now 8 3/4 after the 7 3/4 of the 13th). FIFTH DAY OF THE AUGUST 14-19 BREAK, with the break row ending tomorrow -- that end date is still an intention rather than a record and wants correcting to whatever actually ran. No training today. THE DAY IS COMPLETE AND THE MORNING HALF OF THIS NOTE WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It was written after lunch, at 1,475 kcal and 70.0 g protein, and predicted that dinner would close to roughly 135 g of protein at best while calories landed near the 2,800 target. Dinner was a wedding at Beckta -- gem caesar, flank steak, milk chocolate creme brulee, a slice of dark chocolate raspberry cake, three small slices of bread and whipped butter -- and came to about 2,364 kcal and 77.2 g protein against the 1,325 and 90 the morning note assumed. The day finished at 3,839 kcal and 147.2 g protein: 1,039 OVER the calorie target and 12.8 g under the protein floor. THIS IS THE HIGHEST CALORIE DAY IN THE LOG, across all fifteen logged days, and by a wide margin -- 852 above the previous high of 2,987 on August 11. It is also the best protein day of the break by 40 g, beating the 106.7 of the 17th, and it still missed the floor. That is the composition finding in its sharpest form yet: five trip days have run 95.6, 94.0, 91.0, 106.7 and 147.2 against a 160 g floor, and the one day that ate 3,800 calories was not enough. 147.2 does not reach the top five protein days overall, all of which are pre-trip and run 182 to 216 on fewer calories. Sodium came to 4,806 mg, second-highest in the log behind the 5,864 of August 7, driven by the caesar (1,250, bacon lardons and pecorino) and the steak plate (900). SIX OF THE TEN ROWS ARE ESTIMATES AND ALL SIX DINNER ROWS ARE. The plated courses were built from the printed menu with portions unobserved and carry roughly a 30% band; the cake and the bread are softer still, both assumed weights. Only the Gatorade bar is a published panel. NO BEVERAGES ARE LOGGED: the menu states beverages are additional and none were reported, so if there was wine at the table this total is a floor.
